summary: An array stores several values in order under one name. You get each value by its index, starting at 0.
notes: scores[0] is the first value. scores[scores.length - 1] is the last.
scores.length has no parentheses. It is a property, not a method.
push() adds a value to the end, and length grows by 1.
pitfall: Using scores[scores.length] gives undefined with no error. Doing math with it gives NaN, so the bug shows up later in a different line.
contrast: A JavaScript array can grow like a Python list, and its size is scores.length with no parentheses, like a Java array. Reading past the end gives undefined instead of an error.
